```{r setup}
library(longlineTypology)

## Base-R build: dplyr, lubridate and here are not required.
list2env(params, envir = .GlobalEnv)

if (outdir == "") outdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "cluster_outputs")
dir.create(outdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

stat_list <- list()
```

This document demonstrates clustering of operational longline data to identify
fishing typologies. By default it runs on a small bundled mock dataset; for a
real analysis, point `data_path` to the output of the `seafisheries`
processing pipeline (same format), e.g.

```{r render_example, eval = FALSE}
rmarkdown::render("clusters.Rmd",
                  params = list(scenario  = "sp_hbf_latabs",
                                data_path = "path/to/LL_EC_LF.RDS",
                                outdir    = "cluster_outputs/"))
```

Summary:

- Recomputes species fractions for the species used by the scenario
- Selects relevant variables for clustering and filters invalid hbf / length rows
- Fits the scaling and the PCA on the rows inside a fit window of years, then
  projects every row (inside and outside the window) with those same parameters
- Uses the gap statistic over bootstrap replicates to find candidate numbers of
  clusters K
- Runs kmeans on the fit-window rows for every candidate K, assigns every row
  to the nearest centroid, and records an ordering of the clusters by
  yellowfin catch
- Saves a diagnostics object that downstream reports read (no dataset inside)

# Load dataset

```{r load_dataset}
if (data_path == "") {
	data_path <- system.file("extdata", "mockdata", "LL_mock.RDS",
							 package = "longlineTypology")
}

EC_clean <- readRDS(data_path)
stat_list$nrow_total <- nrow(EC_clean)
```

The mock data (generated by `data-raw/make_mock.R` in the package sources) are
simulated from four fishing strategies with distinct species composition,
latitude band, hooks between floats and fish length, so the clustering has
structure to find. They span 1960 to 2023 and follow the `seafisheries` output
format.

# Define clustering parameters

```{r parameter_values}
# PCA parameters
pca_method             <- "n_components" # "threshold" or "n_components"
pca_variance_threshold <- 0.7            # Used only when pca_method = "threshold"

# kmeans / gap statistic parameters (sized for the mock data; for the full
# dataset use e.g. sample_no = 20000, nstart = 30)
sample_no              <- 100   # Sample size per replicate for gap statistic
kmeans_set             <- 15    # Number of kmeans replicates
max_k                  <- 20    # Maximum number of clusters to test
iter_max               <- 1e6   # Maximum iterations for kmeans
nstart                 <- 10    # Number of random starts for kmeans
B_var                  <- 25    # Bootstrap replicates for gap statistic
ncores                 <- 1     # Number of cores used by fastClusGap (Unix only)

# Years used to FIT the scaling, the PCA and kmeans. Rows outside this range
# are not used for fitting but are still projected and assigned to clusters.
fit_year_min           <- 1990
fit_year_max           <- 2022
```

How the number of principal components is chosen:

- `n_pc > 0` (parameter): manual override, clamped to the number of PCs the
  scenario provides.
- `pca_method = "n_components"`: `nSpeciesComponents()` keeps one component
  fewer than the number of species in the scenario (the species fractions sum
  to 1, so one of them is redundant), with a minimum of 2.
- `pca_method = "threshold"`: keeps enough components to explain
  `pca_variance_threshold` of the variance.

# Select and prepare variables

`selectScenario()` turns the scenario string into column names. Tokens are
joined with `_`, e.g. `yba` (yellowfin, bigeye, albacore), `ybas` (+ skipjack),
`sp` (yellowfin, bigeye, albacore, others), `hbf`, `len`, `lat`, `latabs`,
`lon`.

`recalcSpeciesFractions()` recomputes `total_n` and the fractions so that the
fractions of the species *used by the scenario* sum to 1 in every row.

The z-score parameters (mean and sd of each variable) are computed on the
fit-window rows only, then applied to every row with `applyScaleParams()`, so
that all rows share one scale and rows outside the window do not influence the
fit.

```{r select_prepare_vars}
EC_clean <- recalcSpeciesFractions(EC_clean, scenario)

pca_select <- selectScenario(scenario)

uses_hbf <- any(c("mean_hbf", "hbf_cat") %in% pca_select)
uses_len <- "mean_len" %in% pca_select

if (uses_hbf) {
	stopifnot("hbf_outlier" %in% names(EC_clean))
	EC_clean <- EC_clean[EC_clean$hbf_outlier == "valid", , drop = FALSE]
}
if (uses_len) {
	stopifnot("len_source" %in% names(EC_clean))
	EC_clean <- EC_clean[EC_clean$len_source != "imputed", , drop = FALSE]
}
stat_list$nrow_after_validity_filter <- nrow(EC_clean)

cat("Variables selected for clustering:\n")
print(pca_select)
cat("Rows retained after hbf/len validity filtering:", nrow(EC_clean), "\n")

select_dat <- EC_clean[, pca_select]

# Rows used for fitting (scaling + PCA + kmeans)
yrs     <- as.integer(format(EC_clean$ymd, "%Y"))
idx_fit <- which(yrs >= fit_year_min & yrs <= fit_year_max)
cat("Rows used for fitting (", fit_year_min, "-", fit_year_max, "): ",
	length(idx_fit), " of ", nrow(EC_clean), "\n", sep = "")

# 1) Z-score parameters (mean, sd) computed on the fit rows only
pca_scaled_fit <- pcaScale(select_dat[idx_fit, , drop = FALSE], method = "zscore")
scale_params   <- attr(pca_scaled_fit, "scale_params")

# 2) Apply those SAME parameters to every row, so all rows share one scale
pca_scaled <- applyScaleParams(select_dat, scale_params)
```

# Principal Component Analysis

The PCA is fitted on the fit-window rows, then every row is projected into it
with `predict()`.

```{r pca}
# 3) Fit the PCA on the fit rows only
pca_res <- customPCA(pca_scaled[idx_fit, , drop = FALSE],
					 variance_threshold = pca_variance_threshold,
					 print_it = FALSE)

max_pc <- ncol(pca_res$x)

if (n_pc > 0) {
	if (n_pc != round(n_pc)) stop("n_pc must be an integer, got ", n_pc)
	n_pc_used <- as.integer(n_pc)
	if (n_pc_used < 2) stop("n_pc must be >= 2, got ", n_pc_used)
	if (max_pc < 2) stop("Scenario '", scenario, "' yields only ", max_pc,
						 " PC(s); at least 2 are required")
	if (n_pc_used > max_pc) {
		warning("n_pc = ", n_pc_used, " exceeds the ", max_pc,
				" PCs available for scenario '", scenario,
				"'; clamping to ", max_pc)
		n_pc_used <- max_pc
	}
	pca_res$no_var <- n_pc_used
	cat("PCA retained", pca_res$no_var, "components (manual override, requested",
		n_pc, "of", max_pc, "available)\n\n")
} else if (pca_method == "n_components") {
	pca_res$no_var <- nSpeciesComponents(scenario, min_components = 2)
	cat("PCA retained", pca_res$no_var, "components\n\n")
} else {
	cat("PCA retained", pca_res$no_var, "components explaining >=",
		pca_variance_threshold * 100, "% of variance\n\n")
}

# 4) Project EVERY row (fit rows and rows outside the fit window) into that PCA.
#    pca_res$x only holds the fit rows, so it can't be used for all rows.
pca_full <- predict(pca_res, newdata = pca_scaled)[, 1:pca_res$no_var, drop = FALSE]

# Rows with missing values can't be assigned to a centroid
bad <- !stats::complete.cases(pca_full)
if (any(bad))
	stop(sum(bad), " rows have NA PC scores (missing values in ",
		 paste(pca_select, collapse = ", "), "); filter them before the PCA")

# Clustering set = the fit rows
indices_90  <- idx_fit
pca_full_90 <- pca_full[indices_90, , drop = FALSE]

# Sanity check: projected fit rows must equal the PCA's own scores
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(pca_full_90),
						   unname(pca_res$x[, 1:pca_res$no_var, drop = FALSE]))))

cat("Using", nrow(pca_full_90), "observations from", fit_year_min, "to",
	fit_year_max, "for clustering;", nrow(pca_full) - nrow(pca_full_90),
	"other rows are only assigned to the centroids\n")
stat_list$nrow_clustering <- nrow(pca_full_90)
```

# Determine candidate numbers of clusters

Each replicate draws `sample_no` rows (with replacement) from the fit-window
data and selects K with the gap statistic. Every K selected by at least one
replicate is carried forward; the choice between them is left to the
diagnostic report.

```{r optim_k}
set.seed(123)
sample_indices <- lapply(1:kmeans_set, function(x) {
	sample(1:nrow(pca_full_90), size = sample_no, replace = TRUE)
})

cat("\nRunning", kmeans_set, "kmeans replicates on samples of",
	sample_no, "observations...\n")

kmeans_res <- list()
gap_stat   <- list()

for (i in 1:kmeans_set) {
	pca_sub <- pca_full_90[sample_indices[[i]], 1:pca_res$no_var]

	res <- customKmeans(pca_sub,
						max_k      = max_k,
						random_set = B_var,
						iter_max   = iter_max,
						nstart     = nstart,
						d.power    = 2,
						ncores     = ncores,
						print_it   = FALSE)

	kmeans_res[[i]] <- res$kmeans
	gap_stat[[i]]   <- res$gap_stat
}

# K selected by each replicate
cluster_counts <- data.frame(
	cluster_n = sapply(kmeans_res, function(x) length(unique(x$cluster))),
	replicate = 1:kmeans_set
)

freq_table <- table(cluster_counts$cluster_n)

# Store as data frame for use in diagnostic report
freq_df <- data.frame(
	n_clusters = as.numeric(names(freq_table)),
	freq       = as.numeric(freq_table)
)

cat("\nCluster number distribution across replicates:\n")
print(freq_table)
```

# Apply clustering

For each candidate K, kmeans is fitted on the fit-window data, and every row
(including rows outside the fit window) is assigned to the nearest centroid
with `assignClusters()`. Results are stored as `cluster_k<K>` columns, with the
labels kmeans returned.

The clusters are also ranked by total yellowfin catch in weight
(`orderClusters(by = "yft_w")`). The ranking is stored as an `old` to `new`
lookup per K in `cluster_reorder`; the `cluster_k<K>` columns themselves are
not relabelled.

```{r kmeans}
unique_ks <- sort(unique(cluster_counts$cluster_n))

kmeans_full     <- list()
cluster_reorder <- list()

for (k in unique_ks) {
	cat("\nRunning kmeans on full dataset with K =", k, "\n")

	res_k <- kmeans(pca_full_90, centers = k, iter.max = iter_max, nstart = nstart)

	raw_cluster <- assignClusters(as.data.frame(pca_full),
								  as.data.frame(res_k$centers))

	col_name <- paste0("cluster_k", k)
	EC_clean[[col_name]] <- as.integer(raw_cluster)
	kmeans_full[[as.character(k)]] <- res_k

	# Ranking of the clusters by total yellowfin catch in weight
	ordered_k <- orderClusters(data.frame(cluster = EC_clean[[col_name]],
										  yft_w   = EC_clean$yft_w),
							   by = "yft_w")
	old_ids   <- attr(ordered_k, "old_ids")
	cluster_reorder[[as.character(k)]] <- data.frame(old = old_ids,
													 new = seq_along(old_ids))
}

cat("\nAdded columns:", paste0("cluster_k", unique_ks, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Cluster summary per K

```{r final_cluster_summary, results = "asis"}
diag_tables <- list()

for (k in unique_ks) {
	tmp <- EC_clean
	tmp$cluster <- tmp[[paste0("cluster_k", k)]]

	summary_k <- summaryClusters(tmp)

	cluster_sizes       <- table(tmp$cluster)
	summary_k$n_obs     <- as.numeric(cluster_sizes[match(summary_k$cluster, names(cluster_sizes))])
	summary_k$pct_data  <- summary_k$n_obs / nrow(tmp) * 100

	diag_tables[[as.character(k)]] <- summary_k

	replicate_support <- freq_df$freq[freq_df$n_clusters == k]
	if (length(replicate_support) == 0) replicate_support <- 0

	betweenss_ratio <- kmeans_full[[as.character(k)]]$betweenss /
		kmeans_full[[as.character(k)]]$totss

	cat("\n### K =", k, "\n\n")
	cat("Replicate support:", replicate_support, "/", kmeans_set, "  \n")
	cat("Between-cluster SS / total SS:", round(betweenss_ratio, 3), "\n\n")
	print(knitr::kable(
		summary_k[, c("cluster", "n_obs", "pct_data", "yft_n", "total_n",
					  "yft_catch", "yft_frac")],
		format    = "simple",
		col.names = c("Cluster", "N", "% of Data", "YFT Caught", "Total Catch",
					  "% of Total", "% YFT in Cluster"),
		digits    = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1)
	))
	cat("\n")
}
```

# Save outputs

The diagnostics object holds everything a downstream report needs, without the
dataset itself: run metadata, the scaling and PCA parameters to project new
data, the kmeans fits per K, the gap-statistic replicates, the cluster
assignment per row and the cluster ordering per K.

```{r save_outputs}
# pca_res$x is the per-row score matrix of the fit rows, and reconstructable
# via predict(pca_res_light, newdata = applyScaleParams(<new data>, scale_params)),
# which only needs rotation/center/scale, not $x.
pca_res_light <- pca_res
pca_res_light$x <- NULL

diagnostics <- list(

	# run metadata
	scenario     = scenario,
	pca_method   = pca_method,
	pca_variance_threshold = if (pca_method == "threshold") pca_variance_threshold else NA,
	pca_select   = pca_select,      # variable names -- don't recover via rotation rownames, fragile
	n_components = pca_res$no_var,  # PCs actually used (after any clamping)
	n_pc_requested = n_pc,          # 0 = no override; otherwise the requested value
	n_pc_available = max_pc,

	# training data footprint: lets a future run check "does new data still
	# look like what this was fit on" without opening the raw file
	train_nrow       = nrow(EC_clean),
	train_nrow_1990  = nrow(pca_full_90),           # rows inside the fit window
	train_date_range = range(EC_clean$ymd),
	fit_years        = c(fit_year_min, fit_year_max), # rows used to fit scaling/PCA/kmeans

	# apply the same PCA to new/future data
	scale_params = scale_params,    # mean/sd per raw variable, from the fit rows
	pca_res      = pca_res_light,   # rotation + center + scale, for predict()

	# cluster identity -- assign new data to these same clusters later
	kmeans_full  = kmeans_full,     # named list keyed by K; centers live in each element

	# reproduce the gap statistic / centroid variability / silhouette / Dunn
	gap_stat       = gap_stat,      # per-replicate gap tables -> gap statistic plot
	kmeans_res     = kmeans_res,    # per-replicate kmeans fits -> centroid variability
	sample_indices = sample_indices,# exact rows sampled per replicate -> silhouette/Dunn need the *same* subsample
	freq_df        = freq_df,       # K frequency across replicates

	# cluster assignment, without the dataset itself
	cluster_k = EC_clean[, grep("^cluster_k", names(EC_clean)), drop = FALSE],

	# cluster ordering by total yellowfin catch in weight: named list keyed
	# by K, each a data.frame(old = cluster_k<K> label, new = rank)
	cluster_reorder = cluster_reorder
)

saveRDS(diagnostics, file.path(outdir, "cluster_diagnostics.RDS"))
cat("\nSaved diagnostics to", file.path(outdir, "cluster_diagnostics.RDS"), "\n")
```
